"description": "

This note gives two precise answers associated with Fuchs Conjecture 3.2. The imported bare endpoint-angle condition is false: exactly the two proper face diagonals per initial face and vertex are additional paths and have graph distance two. An explicitly adopted parity-selected convention has a complete unbounded endpoint-exclusion proof through double-pentagon germ symmetry, a physical edge-midpoint half-turn, and a unique-common-neighbor argument. The convention is a supported disambiguation, not an authenticated author correction or uniquely compelled printed reading.

The midpoint and refolding mechanisms are credited to Athreya\u2013Aulicino\u2013Hooper and Troubetzkoy. Alper Ferudun\u2019s current contemporaneous preprint, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23267641, contains both the formulation distinction and endpoint theorem, and the public face-word type correction. GitHub records our draft PR creation on 1 October 2026 and DataCite records that related DOI registration on 9 October 2026. These dates do not establish historical exact-byte visibility, firstness, author awareness or independence. Current website files could not be compared to its DOI-deposited files, and journal/body-version gaps remain disclosed. No current openness or guaranteed novelty is claimed.

The deposit includes a four-page research note, standalone LaTeX source and an exact verification package with current optimization-safe guards, meaningful wrong-science controls, distinct independent scientific audits and bounded priority ledgers. It independently validates the public face word while separating its terminal-angle error and additional displayed-coordinate norm inconsistency. Finite checks corroborate the data; they do not replace the universal proof. AI tools were used extensively in development, drafting, source checking, reproduction and adversarial verification. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review.
